issues.body: mergeNTriples unions independently returned N-Triples documents by exact line and explicitly assumes that the same blank-node label across runs identifies the same node. Blank-node labels are document/result scoped, however, and CONSTRUCT template blank nodes are fresh for each solution and execution. Two expansion runs can both serialize unrelated fresh nodes as (for example) _:b0; concatenating/deduplicating their lines then turns them into one node and may also discard a distinct triple whose serialized text happens to match. This makes the accumulated graph semantically incorrect.
issues.fix_hint: Do not concatenate independently scoped blank-node labels unchanged. Establish an explicit identity policy: at minimum alpha-rename blank nodes with a unique namespace per result document before union so distinct generated nodes cannot collide; if persistent store blank nodes must merge across runs, obtain a stable engine-provided identity/skolemization rather than inferring identity from result-local labels. Add a test merging two documents that both use _:b0 for different structures and assert they remain distinct, plus coverage for the intended same-store-blank-node behavior.
issues.title: Merging independent CONSTRUCT documents can conflate distinct blank nodes

verdict.summary: Round 5 regresses from round 4's zero findings: the lens expansion merge treats blank-node labels from separate CONSTRUCT result documents as globally stable identifiers. RDF blank-node labels are scoped to their result/document, and CONSTRUCT template blank nodes may be freshly allocated on each execution, so exact-line union can silently conflate distinct nodes across start expansions or repeated clicks. The otherwise relevant form-gating, focus-binding, triple-term, and annotation tests do not exercise this cross-result identity invariant.
